1.9.15.en: St. John Chrysostom * He speaks of these Gentiles, that is, of us, who in every place offer sacrifices to Him, that is, the bread of the Eucharist and also the cup of the Eucharist, affirming that we glorify His name, which you (the Jews) defile.

1.9.16.en: St. Justin Martyr * The prophet Malachi, one of the Twelve, foretold: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD of hosts, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen" (Mal 1:10-11). These words indicate in a clear way that the old people (the Jews) will cease to offer offerings to God, but that in every place a pure sacrifice will be offered to Him, and that His name will be glorified among the Gentiles. But what other name is glorified among the Gentiles like that of our Lord, by which the Father and also man are glorified? And because this is the name of His Son, who became flesh by Him, He calls it "his name."

1.9.17.en: St. Irenaeus * It is now the time when the true worshippers worship the Father neither in Jerusalem nor on Mount Gerizim but in spirit and in truth (Jn 4:20-23). Therefore God dwells in the heart. If you are looking for the place of God, the pure heart is His place, for He says by the prophet: "I will dwell in them, and they shall be my people, and I will be their God, saith the Lord" (2 Cor 6:16; Lev 26:12).

1.9.18.en: Origen * It has now been proved from the Holy Scriptures that the Jews lost the inheritance because they rejected Christ, and we who are from the Gentiles have taken their place. Jeremiah says: "I have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage; I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies. Mine heritage is unto me as a lion in the forest; it crieth out against me: therefore have I hated it" (Jer 12:7-8). And also Malachi: "I have no pleasure in you, saith the LORD, neither will I accept an offering at your hand. For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles" (Mal 1:10-11). Isaiah also says: "It shall come, that I will gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come, and see my glory" (Isa 66:18).

1.9.19.en: And he himself says in another place, in the person of the Father to the Son: "I the LORD have called thee in righteousness, and will hold thine hand, and will keep thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles; To open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison, and them that sit in darkness out of the prison house" (Isa 42:6-7).

1.9.20.en: Lactantius * On the Lord's day, gather together to break bread and give thanks, but first confess your sins, that your sacrifice may be pure.

1.9.21.en: In any case, whoever has a dispute with his brother, let him not take part in your gathering until he is reconciled, so that your sacrifice may not be defiled.

1.9.22.en: For this is what the Lord said: "In every place and at every time offer to My name a pure offering, for I am a great King, saith the Lord, and my name is dreadful among the Gentiles" (Mal 1:11).

1.10.0.en: 12 But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the LORD is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible. 13 Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it! and ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering: should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD. 14 But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing: for I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.

1.10.1.en: But ye have profaned it, in that ye say, The table of the LORD is polluted; and the fruit thereof, even his meat, is contemptible. [12]

1.10.2.en: He renews the grave accusation that He had already directed at them in verse 7. Since they violated the divine holy things and the worship, it is no wonder that God drives them away from before Him. They said, not with their mouths but by their conduct, that the table of the Lord is polluted, for they did not lead the people to honor the altar and to offer the finest they had to God, so they became preachers of contempt for the temple of the Lord and His altar.

1.10.3.en: Ye said also, Behold, what a weariness is it!

1.10.4.en: And ye have snuffed at it, saith the LORD of hosts; and ye brought that which was torn, and the lame, and the sick; thus ye brought an offering.

1.11.0.en: Should I accept this of your hand? saith the LORD. [13]

1.11.1.en: The second accusation directed at the priests is that they thought their task heavy and very burdensome, so they fulfilled it in a spirit of grumbling. For this reason the Lord reproaches His people in Micah: "wherein have I wearied thee?" (Mic 6:3), and in Isaiah He says: "I have not caused thee to serve with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense. Thou hast bought me no sweet cane with money, neither hast thou filled me with the fat of thy sacrifices" (Isa 43:23-24).

1.11.2.en: God does not seek the offering but the one who offers the offering. "My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways" (Prov 26:23).

1.11.3.en: Unclean worship turns from the sense of delight and sweetness in fellowship with God into hardship, weariness and boredom, in which man grumbles and is puffed up by his worship instead of enjoying humility. In this way man feels weariness and boredom even in his communal or personal prayers, or his fasting, or his giving, in one form or another.

1.11.4.en: But cursed be the deceiver, which hath in his flock a male, and voweth, and sacrificeth unto the Lord a corrupt thing.

1.12.0.en: For I am a great King, saith the LORD of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen. [14]

1.12.1.en: They offer defective sacrifices, not because suitable sacrifices are lacking, but out of contempt and disdain for the worship of God. They have the best flocks, and what is fit for the service and honor of God, yet they offered the worst they had. They try craftily to present human justifications for offering defective sacrifices. Thus they claim to honor God while they are offending Him.

1.12.2.en: By their craftiness they fell under the curse instead of enjoying the heavenly blessings, for He says of them: "cursed be the deceiver."

1.12.3.en: He rebukes His priests and His people because they behaved in a way that the pagans did not, for His name is great and dreadful among the Gentiles, while the Jews and their priests made light of His name, His temple and His sacrifices. As the psalmist says: "O clap your hands, all ye people... For the LORD most high is terrible; he is a great King over all the earth" (Ps 47:1-2).

1.12.4.en: * It is not enough for Him that one nation be subject to Him; He paid a great price that came out of His side in order to buy the whole world.

1.12.6.en: Sanctify me, that I may offer You a holy sacrifice!

1.12.7.en: * Your voice resounds in the depths of my heart:

1.12.8.en: I have loved you, and chosen you as My son.

1.12.9.en: I redeemed you with My blood that you may enjoy fellowship in My glories!

1.12.10.en: * You chose me before You created me, You knew me before I existed, You prepared glory for me when I was still nothing.

1.12.11.en: What shall I render to You, who anticipate me with Your love?

1.12.12.en: * Take away from me all pride and hypocrisy, for I shall not be justified before You.

1.12.13.en: I have sinned, for I did not honor You as a Father, nor fear You as my Master.

1.12.14.en: Kindle my heart with the fire of Your love, and nail Your fear within me.

1.12.15.en: * In my folly I despised Your name, and offered unclean sacrifices, for I did not offer You the firstfruits of my time, nor give priority to meeting with You.

1.12.16.en: I was busy with temporal things as though they were eternal, and ignored my eternity as though it were an illusion and a fantasy.

1.12.17.en: I have wronged Your long-suffering, O You who await my return to You.

1.12.18.en: * I have sinned, for I was often occupied with formalities, and counted worship of You a heavy duty.

1.12.19.en: Shine upon my heart that it may cleave to You.

1.12.20.en: And let Your Holy Spirit work in me, that I may walk always in the Spirit.

1.12.21.en: * Often I came to You as a lame man, limping between two ways.

1.12.22.en: Carry me to You and in You, O true Way.

1.12.23.en: Take away all sickness from my soul, O heavenly Physician.

1.12.24.en: Lift up my face to You, and let me count all things as refuse for Your sake!

1.12.25.en: * Shine upon me, O Sun of Righteousness, as upon my brethren, that the whole world may be enlightened by Your light.

1.12.26.en: And let all offer pure incense to Your name.

1.12.27.en: And let all enjoy the sacrifice of Your Body and Blood, which were given, and let Your name be glorified in every man!

1.12.28.en: * Turn the whole world into a holy place for You, and let all enjoy fellowship with You, and let all offer a pure, holy sacrifice, as all cleave to the sacrifice of Your Cross.

1.12.29.en: And reign, O heavenly King, over all mankind.

2.0.0.en: 1 And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. 2 If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart. 3 Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it. 4 And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the LORD of hosts.

2.0.1.en: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. [1]

2.0.2.en: Perhaps the priests justify their faults mentioned in the previous chapter by saying that the unclean and defective offerings and sacrifices which they present on the altar are not their fault, but the fault of the people who refuse to give God the best they have. So this chapter comes to uncover what is in the hearts of the priests themselves. The commandment directed here to the priests does not concern offerings and sacrifices but the hearts of the priests, their intentions, their life and their conduct. If the work of the priest is to intercede for the people by offering sacrifices as a type of the sacrifice of the Lord Christ, then it befits the priest to be sanctified. If the priest is not pure, how can his heart cry out for the purity and sanctification of the hearts of others?

2.0.3.en: If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD of hosts, I will even send a curse upon you.

2.1.0.en: And I will curse your blessings: yea, I have cursed them already, because ye do not lay it to heart. [2]

2.1.1.en: God, the Searcher of hearts, knows perfectly that their practice of the priestly work was not for the sake of God's glory; the fault is in the heart itself, therefore the curse comes upon them instead of blessings.

2.1.2.en: Since they do not give their hearts to the Lord, but for the sake of temporal glory or material greed, the curse comes upon them, so that they lose their honor, even the temporal, and their blessings, even the material. They lose what is heavenly, and also what is earthly.

2.1.3.en: * It is a heavy burden that priests are bound to defend the glory of God and work for it, so that we may not appear to neglect any such thing, when God urges us and says: "And now, O ye priests, this commandment is for you. If ye will not hear, and if ye will not lay it to heart, to give glory unto my name, saith the LORD, I will even send a curse upon you, and I will curse your blessings" (cf. Mal 2:1-4).

2.1.4.en: St. Cyprian * When the shepherd walks on steep and rugged places, the flock follows him and falls into the pit of destruction. Hence the Lord grieves over the evil knowledge of the shepherds, and says by the prophet: "Seemeth it a small thing unto you to have eaten up the good pasture, but ye must tread down with your feet the residue of your pastures? and to have drunk of the deep waters, but ye must foul the residue with your feet? And as for my flock, they eat that which ye have trodden with your feet; and they drink that which ye have fouled with your feet" (Ezek 34:18-19).

2.1.5.en: It is clear that when the shepherds drink from clear and pure waters, they are refreshed from the spring of truth by their right understanding, but they corrupt the holy contemplation by their evil life when they foul the waters with their feet. It is self-evident that the flock will drink of these polluted waters fouled by these feet, and then refrain from carrying out the teachings it has heard, because it imitates the evil example it sees. The flock longs to do the good that the shepherds say, but it is turned aside by the evil they do, and so it absorbs the mud along with what it drinks, since it draws from a polluted spring.

2.1.6.en: For this reason the prophet wrote saying that the wicked priests have become a snare for the destruction of the people: "Hear ye this, O priests... for judgment is toward you, because ye have been a snare" (Hos 5:1), "the prophet is a snare of a fowler" (Hos 9:8), and the Lord also says by the prophet concerning the shepherds: "and caused the house of Israel to fall into iniquity" (Ezek 44:12).

2.1.7.en: No one does more harm to the Church than those who have the appearance of holiness and its title but behave corruptly.

2.1.9.en: * This is your duty, O bishop: not to ignore the faults of the people nor to make light of the repentant, lest you destroy the Lord's flock through lack of skill, or insult His new name sealed upon His people, and you yourself be rebuked just as the ancient shepherds were rebuked, when God spoke of them through Jeremiah: [Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, they have defiled my portion] (cf. Jer 12:10).

2.1.10.en: The Apostolic Constitutions Since priests fall under the curse, they in turn become a cause of cursing for those among the people who walk with them in the same way.

2.1.11.en: * Let the people not deceive themselves, thinking that they are safe from the contagion of sin while they cleave to a sinful priest and render obedience to their unjust leader, illegitimate in his episcopate. They are blamed by the prophet Hosea: "their sacrifices shall be unto them as the bread of mourners; all that eat thereof shall be polluted" (Hos 9:4). This teaching shows clearly that all share together in the sin of the corruption of the sacrifice of the blasphemous, unjust priest.

2.2.0.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr Behold, I will corrupt your seed, and spread dung upon your faces, even the dung of your solemn feasts; and one shall take you away with it. [3]

2.2.1.en: The aim of the priestly work is to create the joyful heavenly atmosphere among the people, but because of the corruption of their hearts and intentions their life was turned into a cause of bitterness, famine and sorrow among the people.

2.2.2.en: When the spiritual leaders turn aside from holiness, the blessing flees and the curse comes. Just as the earth was cursed because of the sin of our first parents Adam and Eve, so that it brought forth thorns and thistles, the prophet Isaiah says: "Because thou hast forgotten the God of thy salvation, and hast not been mindful of the rock of thy strength, therefore shalt thou plant pleasant plants... but the harvest shall flee away in the day of the destroying blow and hopeless sorrow" (Isa 17:10-11). And the prophet Hosea says: "For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind: it hath no stalk: the bud shall yield no meal: if so be it yield, the strangers shall swallow it up" (Hos 8:7). And the prophet Jeremiah: "They have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns" (Jer 12:13).

2.2.3.en: * You reap no fruit from the service of idols, for their sheaves are like ears of wheat scattered by the wind; from the outside they appear to be full of grain, but inside they have no yield.

2.2.4.en: * He says: when you forget the Maker of the good things with you, you sow unfaithfulness and reap ingratitude. Well then, you will reap the fruits of your plantings and your seed.

2.2.5.en: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus The text in the Catholic edition reads: "Behold, I will cut off your arms, and scatter dung upon your faces, the dung of your feasts, and it shall carry you away with it." So instead of the honor, glory and blessing that the priests enjoy as servants of God working for the edification of His people, they become men with their arms cut off, dung is thrown on their faces, and they lose the joy of the feasts.

2.2.6.en: Perhaps he means by the dung here what is in the entrails of the sacrifices when they are washed, for since they offer defective sacrifices with corrupt hearts, instead of receiving portions of the sacrifice to eat as priests of God, God throws its dung on their faces as a sign of the shame that comes upon them, making them despised among the people and base. This is the lot of the servant who seeks not the glory of God but his own glory and his own material gain. They become like a dunghill, fit only to have dung thrown on them.

2.3.0.en: And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you, that my covenant might be with Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. [4]

2.3.1.en: God affirms that what Malachi speaks is not from himself, but is the word of God which He sent to them for their repentance, sending it to them because of His covenant with Levi, that he be sanctified for the sake of the divine service.

2.3.2.en: In all generations the Lord wishes to establish with His children and His people an everlasting covenant, that they may enjoy the heavenly inheritance. As the psalmist says: "He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations" (Ps 105:8).

2.3.3.en: * After saying "He hath remembered his covenant for ever," which we must understand as a covenant that remains forever, the covenant of justification and eternal inheritance, which God promises through faith, he added: "the word which he commanded to a thousand generations." What does he mean by the word "commanded"? The commandment here is faith, by which the just shall live (Rom 1:17), and the eternal inheritance is set over against this faith.

2.3.4.en: St. Augustine * "They kept not the covenant of God, and refused to walk in his law; and forgat his works, and his wonders that he had shewed them" (Ps 78:9-10). They rebelled against Him who renewed them in Baptism... He divided the sea and caused them to pass through it, and made the waters stand as in a vessel. And He led them with a cloud in the daytime (Ps 78:12-14).

2.3.5.en: * "My mercy will I keep for him for evermore, and my covenant shall stand fast with him" (Ps 89:28). He keeps His mercy continually in the Church, which He saves by the covenant of His commandments.

2.3.6.en: * The Law was merely the beginning of the covenant, and the Gospel is its completion.

2.4.0.en: 5 My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me, and was afraid before my name. 6 The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. 7 For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts.

2.4.1.en: When God established His covenant with the sons of Levi, especially with Aaron and his sons, He did not lay a heavy yoke upon them. He offered a covenant "of life and peace." God set them apart to be a cause of life for His people, and of peace for them, through their holy service.

2.4.2.en: If God made a covenant with His people, He made it in particular with the tribe of Levi. "For the LORD had spoken unto Moses, saying, Only thou shalt not number the tribe of Levi, neither take the sum of them among the children of Israel: But thou shalt appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of testimony... they shall bear the tabernacle, and all the vessels thereof, and they shall minister unto it, and shall encamp round about the tabernacle" (Num 3:12). As He also said to him: "And take thou unto thee Aaron thy brother, and his sons with him, from among the children of Israel, that he may minister unto me in the priest's office" (Ex 28:1), as it is said: "Aaron the saint of the LORD" (Ps 106:16).

2.4.3.en: God opens the doors of heaven to pour out upon the soul that fears the Lord and bears His fear within. He grants us eternal life and inner peace if we fear Him.

2.4.4.en: My covenant was with him of life and peace; and I gave them to him for the fear wherewith he feared me.

2.4.5.en: And was afraid before my name. [5]

2.4.6.en: The priest is entrusted with the divine covenant that he may be the messenger of the LORD of hosts, the messenger of the covenant of life and peace. When Moses blessed the tribes before his departure he said of Levi: "Who said unto his father and to his mother, I have not seen him; neither did he acknowledge his brethren, nor knew his own children: for they have observed thy word, and kept thy covenant" (Deut 33:9). So it befitted Levi, as a servant of the Holy One, to concentrate all his energies on the divine commandment and the divine covenant above every relationship, until he seemed as one who does not see his father and mother, does not acknowledge his brethren, and does not know his children.

2.4.7.en: What does He mean by saying: "My covenant was with him of life and peace"?

2.4.8.en: If eternal death has come upon man because of sin, and he has lost his inner peace and his peace with God and with his brethren, because he turned his back to God, the giver of peace, then the aim of the divine covenant is to raise the spiritually dead to enjoy Christ "the Resurrection," so that man lives and does not die, and reconciliation takes place between him and God, so that he is filled with peace within himself as well as with his brethren. This is the work of the priest, with which he ought to be occupied and from which he ought not to turn aside.

2.4.9.en: * He saved mankind, the work of His hands, and not any other work; that is, what He created for Himself He saved for Himself. He created man who perished through his evil. He (the Lord Christ) died in order to keep man for Himself by His right hand.

2.4.10.en: * He is the Lord who says: "My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready." I am ready here, and I am ready in the life to come. I am a Savior on earth, I am a Savior in heaven. I give eternal life to angels and men together.

2.4.11.en: St. Jerome The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips.

2.5.0.en: He walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity. [6]

2.5.1.en: It befits the priest to have knowledge of heavenly things, to live them and bear witness to them before the people, so that he brings forth out of his treasure things new and old (Mt 13:52).

2.6.0.en: For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts. [7]

2.6.1.en: Solomon the Wise sees that the priest must be wise, so that his lips overflow with words of knowledge and wisdom, by which he draws many to the way of truth, for he says: "In the lips of him that hath understanding wisdom is found... The lips of the righteous guide many" (Prov 10:13-21).

2.6.2.en: Nothing occupies the priest's heart but the Law, or the divine commandment, and his lips utter nothing but what accords with the Law: "they should seek the law at his mouth." All that he utters is ascribed to the One who commissioned him, who sent him, "for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" [7].

2.6.3.en: It befits the priest to realize his position as the messenger of the LORD of hosts, having a true, heavenly, divine vision. As the Lord said to the prophet Isaiah: "Go, set a watchman, let him declare what he seeth" (Isa 21:6). It befits the priest to cry out to God, saying: "My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights" (Isa 21:8). Thus the priest stands night and day, knowing no rest for his body, looking continually upon his people as with the eyes of the Lord, in the midst of their joys as by day and all the nights in the midst of their afflictions. He cares for them while the Sun of Righteousness shines upon them, as he cares for their salvation when the darkness of night comes upon them because of their turning away from the Sun of Righteousness.

2.6.4.en: Moreover it befits the believer, for his part, while seeking the counsel of the LORD of hosts, to resort to prayer and supplication, together with asking "the messenger of the LORD of hosts," and not to cease seeking knowledge and the divine will.

2.6.5.en: * The work of a messenger is this, to pass on from one to another what he has been told. For this reason the priest too is called a messenger (Mal 2:7), because he does not speak his own words, but the words of him who sends him.

2.6.6.en: St. John Chrysostom * We must fear lest the prophet's violent rebuke be directed at us: "dumb dogs, they cannot bark" (Isa 56:10). By the barking of dogs and the shepherd's staff the ferocity of wolves is resisted. Now surely priests are not ordained to be stewards of fields or sowers of lands, but to be tillers of souls, which the Apostle surely speaks of when he said: "I have planted, Apollos watered." And again he said: "For we are labourers together with God: ye are God's husbandry" (1 Cor 3:9). These truths must be received with great fear by all priests, who cannot be ignorant of the divine law and the canonical regulations, as the Apostle says: [If anyone belongs to the Lord, let him know what I say; but if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant] (cf. 1 Cor 14:37-38). For this reason, let him fear completely what the Lord said by the prophet: "Therefore my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge" (Isa 5:13). Besides this: "He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer shall be abomination" (Prov 28:9). "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge" (Mal 2:7). It is written concerning the priests' garments that when they enter the temple there must be golden bells on the hems of the garments. What are these but that when all the priests of the Lord enter the Church they do not cease to cry out, that is, to preach about the last things, the end of the world and the coming judgment? By their continual proclamation of the rewards of the righteous and the punishments of the wicked, they urge the good to what is better, and turn the wicked from their sinful conduct through fear of the coming judgment.

2.6.7.en: Father Caesarius, bishop of Arles * Nothing holy was formerly offered or practiced in the temple without the priest. For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth, "for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts," as the prophet says (Mal 2:7).

2.6.8.en: The Didascalia * It was said to sinners: "Thy prophets have seen vain and foolish things for thee: and they have not discovered thine iniquity, to turn away thy captivity" (Lam 2:14). It is to be noted that teachers were sometimes called "prophets" in the Holy Scripture, because they showed the nature of the present and announced the future. It is as though God accuses them of lying if they praise the doers of evil and acquit them instead of condemning their faults, and that out of fear of them.

2.6.9.en: If shepherds avoid using words of rebuke, they fail to disclose the faults of the wicked. For words of rebuke are truly the key that reveals the sin which the one who commits it often does not feel. For this reason the Apostle Paul says: "Holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers" (Titus 1:9), and Malachi also says: "For the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of the LORD of hosts" (Mal 2:7). Therefore the Lord warns on the lips of Isaiah, saying: "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet" (Isa 58:1). He who enters the priesthood takes the office of a messenger who cries with a loud voice, and goes before the coming of the just Judge, who follows him with a terrible appearance.

2.7.s.en: 3. Their corrupting the covenant with God:

2.7.0.en: 8 But ye are departed out of the way; ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. 9 Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law.

2.7.1.en: Ye have caused many to stumble at the law.

2.7.2.en: Ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. [8]

2.7.3.en: "Ye have caused many to stumble at the law" [8], either by their interpreting the Law in a literal, killing way, so that it became a burden on the soul, or by applying it as they please for the sake of their personal interests, flattering the rich and being harsh on the poor and the weak. These turn even the Gospel of Christ, which is a savor of life unto life, into "a savour of death unto death" (2 Cor 2:16), and the Lord Christ Himself becomes to them a "rock of offence" (Rom 9:33).

2.7.4.en: It is a cause of stumbling for the people that the priest turn aside from the way, and betray the covenant that God established with Levi. What is turning aside from the divine way but the priest's being occupied with something other than the salvation of his own soul and the salvation of his children or the people? This is the way of the Lord, who wants all to be saved and to come to the knowledge of God. Thus they corrupt the covenant with God the Lover of mankind.

2.7.5.en: * The just Judge disowns them and ignores them, for those whose trials and sufferings He eases in this world are in truth rejected by Him. Therefore the Lord of glory says to such as these, even if they perform miracles: "I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity" (Lk 13:27; Mt 7:23). The voice of divine truth rebukes the folly of such shepherds, saying: "they are shepherds that cannot understand" (Isa 56:11). Again the Lord reproves them, saying: "they that handle the law knew me not" (Jer 2:8). And therefore divine truth complains of these shepherds because they did not know Him. For no one understands the loftiness of the service of leadership except those who know Him, but those who are ignorant of what belongs to the Lord, the Lord ignores them, as the Apostle Paul says: "But if any man be ignorant, let him be ignorant" (1 Cor 14:38).

2.7.6.en: * The unworthiness of the shepherd is often joined with the unworthiness of the flock, so if the shepherds do not possess the light of knowledge as a result of their personal sin, the flock accordingly stumbles because of its ignorance, according to the punishment of judgment. For this reason the Lord of glory Jesus said: "And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch" (Mt 15:14; Lk 6:39). In this the psalmist said prophetically: "Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake" (Ps 69:23). The leaders are in truth eyes, for they are at the front of the highest ranks and have undertaken to make the way plain, while those who follow them are bound to them and are therefore called "loins." Thus when the eyes are darkened the loins also are bent, for when the leaders lose the light of knowledge, those who follow them bow down under the yoke of their sins.

2.7.8.en: * So the priestly ministry is a trade. Therefore the prophet says to the children of Israel: [Your tavern-keepers mix water with their wine] (cf. Isa 1:22) LXX. St. Isaiah is not speaking of tavern-keepers who in their turn, in their service of the taverns, adulterate pure wine with water. It is difficult to think that this blessed man is speaking of this matter as if he were a civil judge concerned that people dilute strong drink with water. Rather he speaks of tavern-keepers who dwell not in taverns but in churches. These do not offer the thirsty a cup of passions but of virtue. They do not serve the cup of strong drink but the cup of the Savior. He rebukes these tavern-keepers and criticizes them, complaining that they mix the wine with water. This is what he criticizes in them: that though they were appointed for the divine works, they became occupied with human affairs, as the prophet himself says: "Every one is busy with his own house." For if a priest neglects the priestly work and is immersed in worldly pleasures, he mixes the wine with water, that is, he mixes warm things with trivial, cold things.

2.7.9.en: Father Maximus, bishop of Turin It is dangerous for the shepherd to lose the spirit of discernment, so that the word meant for enlightenment turns into a stumbling block for the people, as the Lord Christ said: "They be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch" (Mt 15:14). And the prophet Isaiah says: "We grope for the wall like the blind, and as they that have no eyes we feel our way; we have stumbled at noonday as in darkness, in the mist as dead men" (Isa 59:9-10).

2.7.10.en: * They read the Holy Scripture, and do not see the truth in it, and they resemble the blind who walk feeling the wall without seeing. And they fall at noon as at midnight. You see what misery this is for all. Although the Sun of Righteousness shines on the whole world, they (the Jews) stumble and fall as in the death of night. They sigh like a dead person. They spend life in great sorrow so that their existence seems like death.

2.7.11.en: Theodoret, bishop of Cyrus * They are blind leaders of a blind people. Who are these blind leaders? The Pharisees, whose minds the god of this age blinded, because they do not believe, since they did not believe in Jesus Christ. The god of this age has blinded them so that the light of the gospel of the glory of God in the face of Christ should not shine on them (2 Cor 4:4). We must avoid being led by these blind persons. It befits us not only to do this but also to listen carefully to those who are engaged in leadership in the way of sound teaching, and to apply with right judgment what they say. Let us do this so that we ourselves may not appear blind, because we do not see the meaning of the Holy Scriptures.

2.8.0.en: Origen Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people, according as ye have not kept my ways, but have been partial in the law. [9]

2.8.1.en: Since the people perceive in the priests that instead of being a source of divine blessing, they have come to bear the curse [2], therefore the Lord says: "Therefore have I also made you contemptible and base before all the people" [9].

2.8.2.en: Besides turning aside from the divine way and corrupting the covenant, they are partial in the law. They choose from it what they please, and ignore what does not accord with their evil will. They fulfill the outward appearances, and do not care about inner purity. They do not respect all His commandments. The psalmist says: "Then shall I not be ashamed, when I have respect unto all thy commandments" (Ps 119:6).

2.8.3.en: Perhaps by partiality in the law he means their using the commandment in partiality toward persons, flattering some and being harsh to others, not with wisdom for their salvation but to achieve personal interests, whereas "there is no respect of persons with God" (Rom 2:11). As Elihu says: "How much less to him that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all are the work of his hands" (Job 34:19).

2.9.s.en: 4. Corrupting the covenant with one's neighbor:

2.9.0.en: Have we not all one father?

2.9.1.en: Hath not one God created us?

2.9.2.en: Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers? [10]

2.9.3.en: They ignored their brethren as sons of one heavenly Father and creatures made by one God, so each of them dealt treacherously with his brother. Since they do not love God they do not love their brethren, and also by dealing treacherously with one another they insult the Father of all and the Creator of all. The Apostle Paul says: "One God and Father of all" (Eph 4:6), and the prophet Isaiah says: "But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand" (Isa 64:8).

2.9.4.en: * There (in heaven) there is no love with special regard for a neighbor, but all will love one another abundantly in one pattern. There they neither marry wives nor beget children, and there is no distinction between male and female, but all will be sons of their Father who is in heaven, as the prophet said: "Have we not all one father? hath not one God created us?" (Mal 2:10).

2.9.5.en: * As for what I said, that there will be no wives and no distinction between male and female, our Lord and His apostles taught this. "They which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage: Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of God" (cf. Lk 20:35-36). And the Apostle said: "There is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Gal 3:28).

2.9.6.en: St. Aphrahat * Do you not hear Moses when he says: "You forsook God who begot you" (Deut 32:15) LXX? Do you not hear Malachi rebuking them and saying that "one God created you" and there is "one Father of all" (Mal 2:10) LXX.

2.9.7.en: St. John Chrysostom * This is God's tenderness toward mankind, that He who is the Creator became afterward, according to grace, a Father to them also. He becomes so when the people, His creation, receive Him in their hearts, as the Apostle says: "the Spirit of his Son crying, Abba, Father." These are those who, receiving the Word, obtain from Him authority to become children of God, though by nature they are His creatures, unlike the receiving of the Spirit of the true natural Son. Therefore "the Word was made flesh," that He might make men fit for divinity. The same meaning can be obtained from the prophet Malachi, who says: "Hath not one God created us? have we not all one father?" (Mal 2:10). He put "created" first and then "father," to show, like the other writers, that from the beginning we were creatures by nature. God is our Creator by the Word, but afterward God the Creator became our Father also.

2.9.8.en: St. Athanasius the Apostolic * The Scripture declares the truth, saying: "First of all, believe that there is one God, who created and completed all things, and brought all things from non-being into being," He who contains all things, and Himself is contained by no one. Rightly Malachi also said among the prophets: "Hath not one God created us?" The Apostle also says in agreement with this: "One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in you all" (Eph 4:6). So also the Lord says: "All things are delivered unto me of my Father" (Mt 11:27). It is clear that it is by the One who created all things, since things were not delivered to Him from another, but from what is His own.

2.10.0.en: 11 Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god. 12 The LORD will cut off the man that doeth this, the master and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the LORD of hosts. 13 And this have ye done again, covering the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping, and with crying out, insomuch that he regardeth not the offering any more, or receiveth it with good will at your hand.

2.10.1.en: But ye are departed out of the way; Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem.

2.10.2.en: For Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god. [11]

2.10.3.en: The prophet repeats the word "treachery" and its derivatives five times in this passage [10-16], as though treachery had become a common mark of their life and conduct. The psalmist says: "Let them be ashamed which transgress without cause" (Ps 25:3). He also says: "be not merciful to any wicked transgressors" (Ps 59:5), "I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved; because they kept not thy word" (Ps 119:158). "But the wicked shall be cut off from the earth, and the transgressors shall be rooted out of it" (Prov 2:22), "the perverseness of transgressors shall destroy them" (Prov 11:3). Thus we see how grave is treachery and unfaithfulness to the covenant.

2.10.4.en: * So Paul lamented the Jews (for their treachery), and the Lord grieved over Jerusalem, and the divine Jeremiah lamented the people for their failure to fulfill the Law.

2.10.5.en: * I have sufficient ground S for hope in those who believe in You and enjoy Your help. For You are accustomed to show Your care for them, while You refute those who deal treacherously. It is fitting now to point out that it is not sinners but those who break the Law without cause (in treachery) whom shame covers. Not everyone sins in the same way, for some grieve because of certain circumstances or natural weakness, and others boast of their disobedience and contempt.

2.10.6.en: Theodorus, bishop of Cyrus Treachery here means betrayal of the covenant, for whoever breaks the covenant with God is treacherous and unfaithful in his covenant. This treachery is reflected in his dealings even with the one closest to him, the husband or wife whom he received from God as the partner of his life and a helper to him in all aspects of his life.

2.10.7.en: The sign of the treachery and the abomination is that they insulted their God by marrying pagan women [11] and divorcing their believing wives. He counted these two crimes as directed against Him personally, and as treachery against Him. The first crime is fellowship with unbelievers, where the unbeliever pushes the other party to deny the faith. The second crime is the dissolving of the holy marriage bond that God bound.

2.10.8.en: * If you wish to see more clearly how a Christian woman may by no means marry a Gentile, observe what the Apostle himself says: "The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband be dead, she is at liberty to be married to whom she will; only in the Lord" (1 Cor 7:39), that is, to be a Christian. He who permits a second and a third marriage in the Lord forbids first marriages with a Gentile. For this reason Abraham also made his servant swear on his thigh, that is, by Christ who came from his seed, that he would not bring a foreign woman as wife for his son Isaac (Gen 24:1-9). And Ezra, when he discovered disobedience to God of this kind, made his countrymen put away their wives (Ezra 10:1-17). And the prophet Malachi speaks thus: "Judah hath dealt treacherously, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem; for Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD which he loved, and hath married the daughter of a strange god. The LORD will cut off the man that doeth this, the master and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the LORD of hosts."

2.11.0.en: St. Jerome The LORD will cut off the man that doeth this, the master and the scholar, out of the tabernacles of Jacob, and him that offereth an offering unto the LORD of hosts. [12]

2.11.1.en: By such conduct, by which believers defile the holiness of the Lord, the believers cut off themselves and those who belong to them from the commonwealth of the people of God (Eph 2:12). The "master and the scholar" are also cut off, that is, the teachers and the learners, the blind leaders who fall, they and their followers, into the pit of error.

2.11.2.en: The believer who is married to a pagan is cut off "out of the tabernacles of Jacob," that is, from the people of God; and the priest who "offereth an offering unto the LORD" and commits the same fault falls under the same penalty: being cut off and deprived of the service of the temple of the Lord, and of his priesthood.

2.11.3.en: Because of the people's fornication with the daughters of Moab, who invited the people to idolatrous worship (Num 25:1), Israel joined itself to Baal-peor, and the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel. So Moses killed all the heads of the people who had committed this iniquity. Phinehas the high priest was also zealous with the zeal of God and thrust through with his spear the man who boldly joined himself to a Midianite woman, and the woman. In the same way Nehemiah drove out the grandson of the high priest because he had married a pagan woman (Neh 13:8).

2.11.4.en: The priest Phinehas, in this zeal of his, became a type of the Lord Christ, who delivered Himself to death on the Cross and so removed the divine wrath from those who believe in Him.
